rv.q: But it is an exuberantly inventive evening, one existing in its own right at a tangent to the original, and proving that an ingenious William Rose idea, even when put to a farcical purpose, can still smell as sweet.
The result is a caper that delights, even if it can't disarm.

cn.t: Graham Linehan's stage adaptation of the Ealing classic works well as slapstick farce with contemporary knowingness, though its genre-shifting nature prevents it from reaching the escalating heights of truly great farce.
